# glinet_screen_schedule (Resource)

Manages the schedule of the LCD screen of the router (`timer.get_screen` and `timer.set_screen`): on the scheduled days, the screen turns off at `turn_off_time` and on at `turn_on_time`. The router has one screen schedule, so use one instance of this resource. Only a router with a screen (`hardware_feature.screen` of `system.get_info`) has this setting: on other routers, create and update fail and do not write to the router. The resource works like `glinet_led_schedule`: when `enabled` is `false`, the provider first writes the schedule enabled with the configured times and days, and then disables it. That the router keeps the times and days only from a write that enables the schedule, as for the LED schedule, is not known. The writes are from the web UI code of firmware 4.8.3 and were not tested on a router. Destroy removes the resource from the Terraform state and does not change the router.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# The screen is off from 23:00 to 06:30 on all days.
resource "glinet_screen_schedule" "this" {
  enabled       = true
  turn_off_time = "23:00"
  turn_on_time  = "06:30"
  days          = [0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6]
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `days` (Set of Number) Days of the week when the schedule runs. Each day is a number from 0 (Sunday) to 6 (Saturday) (`week` in the router API).
- `enabled` (Boolean) Whether the schedule is enabled (`enable` in the router API).
- `turn_off_time` (String) Time when the screen turns off (`turnoff_hour` and `turnoff_min` in the router API). Format `HH:MM`, 24 hours, in the time zone of the router.
- `turn_on_time` (String) Time when the screen turns on (`turnon_hour` and `turnon_min` in the router API). It must not be the same as `turn_off_time`, as in the web UI. Format `HH:MM`, 24 hours, in the time zone of the router.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Always `screen_schedule`.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# The import ID is always "screen_schedule".
terraform import glinet_screen_schedule.this screen_schedule
```
